title: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.setRatio off-by-one: setRatio allows newRatio == MAX_RATIO (50) but constructor and docs imply the max settable ratio is MAX_RATIO - 1
description:
The contract documents `MAX_RATIO` (50) as an EXCLUSIVE upper bound: comments on line 29 state 'Exclusive upper bound on `ratio`. Max settable ratio is MAX_RATIO - 1.' and line 47 states the ratio must be `Strictly < MAX_RATIO`. However, `setRatio` uses `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert RatioTooHigh();` — i.e., it ACCEPTS newRatio == MAX_RATIO (50). This is an off-by-one against the documented invariant; the check should be `>= MAX_RATIO` (or `> MAX_RATIO - 1`) to enforce strict-less-than. The bug is also silently exploitable by the owner setting ratio = 50 once: nothing in the contract enforces the invariant going forward.

Note that the constructor sets ratio to `DEFAULT_RATIO = 50` (line 86) — which itself already violates the documented strict-less-than-MAX_RATIO invariant. So in practice the hook is born with ratio == MAX_RATIO and the only way to honour the docs would be for the owner to call setRatio with a value < 50 immediately after deploy. The deploy state is therefore inconsistent with the invariant the code claims to protect.

Economic impact: the documented invariant exists presumably to ensure mintDebt accrual stays below 50% of dispatched USDS notional (so phUSD is always over-collateralised by USDS notional). The off-by-one allows exactly 50% accrual, which is the boundary case — minor in isolation but combined with ECON-RAW-003 the boundary case is the worst-case for debt > realisable-USDC divergence.
exploit_path:
1. Hook deploys with ratio = 50 (= MAX_RATIO), already in violation of the documented strict-less-than invariant.
2. Owner calls setRatio(50); check passes because `50 > 50` is false. Hook now permanently at ratio = MAX_RATIO with no further protection.
3. There is no economic value extraction here per se — the impact is purely that the code does not enforce the documented invariant and a future auditor / external integrator who reads the doc-comment will be misled.
mainnet_realism: Pure on-chain logic; no Balancer-mainnet dependency.
recommendation: Change line 93 from `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert RatioTooHigh();` to `if (newRatio >= MAX_RATIO) revert RatioTooHigh();`. Also change DEFAULT_RATIO from 50 to 49 (or any value < MAX_RATIO) to bring the deploy state into compliance with the documented invariant. Alternatively, if the intent is that ratio==50 IS allowed, update the docstring on line 29 / line 47 to reflect that MAX_RATIO is inclusive.
severity_rationale: Confirmed Low/QA. Pure off-by-one spec/comment mismatch: docstring claims MAX_RATIO is exclusive (max settable = MAX_RATIO - 1) but setRatio uses `> MAX_RATIO` (allowing newRatio == 50). Constructor also sets DEFAULT_RATIO = 50, immediately violating the documented invariant. No direct value extraction — but the boundary case (ratio = 50) is the worst case for the ECON-RAW-003 debt-vs-USDC divergence. Per C4 QA/Low: 'State handling, function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments' — clearly fits Low.
